newsitem.title: USA: U.S. CORPORATE BONDS - Junk firm, Iridium priced.
newsitem.headline: U.S. CORPORATE BONDS - Junk firm, Iridium priced.

text.p: U.S. high-yield bond prices were quoted 1/4 higher on Friday amid lower Treasury yields and an extension of mutual fund cash inflows, traders said, while the much-anticipated Iridium deal priced.

Despite the overall firm tone, Iridium LLC's junk bond offering was faced with another round of restructuring with higher yields. At the same time, Iridium was then able to upsize the deal to $800 million.
Iridium's $500 million 14 percent eight-year senior notes were priced to yield 15 percent, while $300 million 13 percent eight-year senior notes were priced to yield 13-1/2 percent.
The 13 percent notes were priced as units that included warrants to purchase up to a one percent equity stake in Iridium World Communications Ltd.
Traders said there would be no action in the name because of the late pricing by lead manager Chase Securities. But the sector earlier did not let Iridium go unnoticed.

Bonds of Globalstar L.P. dropped as much as one point to boost their yield to comparable levels, traders said. Late in the session, Globalstar's $325 million 11-1/4 percent debt fell 3/4 point to 92-3/4 bid, 93-1/2 offer as traders pushed the yield to 13 percent.

Buysiders were enthused with the deal after the jettison of a $250 million zero coupon tranche and adjustment of yields that were first pegged as low as 12 percent. One manager noted Iridium's leverage ratio was untarnished despite the size of the offering.

"It is not adding more debt to their balance sheet -- all they are doing is taking out of one pocket and putting it into another," said one fund manager at a large New York investment firm. "By locking in this financing, they are eliminating the need for more bank debt, which they already have available."
Away from satellites, high-yield deals were in favor as evidenced by Thursday's $100 million 10-1/2 percent senior subordinated notes, which traded in a 100-1/2 bid, 101 offer market, traders said.

The sixth consecutive week of positive cash flows to U.S. junk bond funds underpinned the tone. Funds reported inflows of $388.6 million in the latest week, compared with inflows of $182.1 million in the prior week, said AMG Data Services.
Next week's junk bond issuance promises to be heavy, with perhaps more than 20 deals coming to market, sources said.

Other high-yield trades on Friday included Grand Union 11s -- sliding further to 65 bid from 66-1/2 -- and Harrah's Jazz notes -- dropping to 32 bid, 34 offer after parent Harrah's Entertainment Inc said it would not extend debtor in posession financing beyond September 30.
Harrah's Jazz in June filed for bankruptcy protection after the Louisiana legislature did not approve terms of its amended casino operating contract.
Turning to high-grades, spreads were called unchanged to firmer reflecting the successful digestion of most of the week's meaty new issue calendar.

Thursday's $1.0 billion global offering from Philip Morris Cos Inc tightened to 78 basis point bid, 77 basis point offer when freed to trade on Friday, better than its initial spread of 79 basis points over the curve.
High liquidity thanks to its international placement ensured a strong market for the bond, a trader said.

U.S. Treasuries closed higher after a record sixth consecutive drop in monthly producer price data extended the long-standing positive inflation outlook. The long bond gained 15/32 to yield 6.53 percent and the 10-year T-note closed up 7/32 to yield 6.22 percent.
